styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Volcanoes, rainforest walks and island day trips.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Markets, seafood and a strong café scene.

stays.why: Walk to the waterfront, ferries and trains. Best base without a car.
Waterfront restaurants and bars on the doorstep; short walk to the CBD.
Cafés, bars and boutiques in a leafy inner suburb; short bus or rideshare to the centre.
Quiet historic village with gardens and the museum nearby; good for families.

food: Try a hangi-style or modern Māori dish, and seafood like green-lipped mussels and fish and chips.
Auckland is famous for brunch. Cafés in Ponsonby and Parnell serve flat whites and big breakfasts.
Night markets (for example in the suburbs) are cheap and good for Asian street food; check which night on the day.
The Viaduct and Britomart have waterfront restaurants; book ahead on weekends.
Supermarkets and food courts keep meal costs down; a casual lunch is often NZ$15–25.
more_time: Take a ferry to Waiheke Island for beaches and vineyards; check ferry times and prices on the day.
Swap a city day for a west-coast beach such as Piha; a rental car or tour is easiest.
Hike a volcano: short walks up Mount Eden or One Tree Hill give city and harbour views.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the harbour, a volcano walk and a ferry trip; add a night for an island or west-coast beach day.

month_notes: January: warmest and driest feel, highs near 23°C. Book ferries and beaches early.
February: similar to January, around 23°C. Great for beaches and island trips.
March: still warm at 22°C, but rain days stay around 11. Pack a light rain jacket.
April: cooler at 20°C. Good for hiking; evenings need a layer.
May: drops to 17°C with more rain days (13). Mix indoor sights with short walks.
June: cool at 15°C and wetter. Bring a waterproof and warm layers.
July: coldest month, highs near 14°C. Indoor museums and cafés are good bets.
August: similar cold, around 14°C, with the most rain days (14). Plan flexible days.
September: still cool at 15°C and the wettest month (15 rain days). Keep an umbrella handy.
October: warms to 17°C but rain days stay high (13). Check forecasts each morning.
November: milder at 19°C. Good shoulder season for walks and ferries.
December: warm again at 21°C. Busy holiday season; book stays ahead.

climate_guide.summary: Mild oceanic climate: warm, drier summers and cool, wetter winters. Rain can come any month.

items.title: Best time: December to March
items.text: Warmest months, highs around 21–23°C. Best for beaches, ferries and volcano walks.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: Expect roughly 11–15 rain days every month. Showers can be short; carry a light rain jacket.

items.title: Cool winters (June to August)
items.text: Highs near 14–15°C and lows around 9–11°C. Bring warm layers and a waterproof.

items.title: Sea breezes and changeable days
items.text: Harbour winds can make it feel cooler. A layer you can add or remove helps.

items.title: Swim in summer
items.text: Water and air are warmest December to March. Other months suit walks more than swims.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a rain jacket, comfortable walking shoes and sunscreen for summer. A warm hat for winter.

transit.best: Walk the CBD and take trains, buses or ferries; use an AT HOP card or contactless card.

modes.text: Four lines run from Waitematā Station, and a new underground city loop is open. Good for suburbs and the airport link via bus or rail; check routes on the day.
Buses cover most suburbs. Cash is not accepted; use an AT HOP card or contactless card. Fares start around NZ$2.80 per zone with free transfers within 30 minutes.
Ferries leave the CBD for Hauraki Gulf islands and Devonport. A quick, scenic way to cross the harbour.
Uber works widely; taxis are plentiful and take cards.
Driving is easy off-peak, but motorways jam at rush hour and parking is hard.
Walking suits the CBD and waterfront. Use transit for hills and far suburbs.
